items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The file has no comments, so the #if 0 / r"""" ... """#" switching trick is never explained, which the conventions ask for. Names are terse: BigInt field `d`, bi helpers, single-letter `a`, `b`, `n` throughout. Formatting is clean.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Functions are short and there is no dead code. But a hand-rolled BigInt (init_bi/add_bi, about 30 lines) is extra complexity beyond the 'clear iterative Fibonacci' the conventions ask for. The redundant `if n <= 0: return 0` guard is duplicated in both languages.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: malloc/realloc results are never checked. The magic constant 1000000000ULL is repeated. C `atol(argv[1])` turns non-numeric input into 0 and prints "0". Negative N prints 0 with exit 0. A missing argument exits 1 with no usage message.

items.name: Boundary and large inputs
items.evidence: Both are iterative and f(0)/f(1) are correct; BigInt is correct far beyond n=93, and a missing argument exits non-zero. But negative N prints 0 with exit 0 in both languages, and C `atol` accepts non-numeric input and prints 0 instead of rejecting it.

items.name: Exact invocation contract
items.evidence: Works with exactly the two given commands and no extra flags. It compiled cleanly even under -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pedantic, and stdout is only the number.
